chief_complaint: burning pain and numbness in bilateral feet in stocking pattern
hpi_details: A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with burning pain and numbness in bilateral feet in stocking pattern. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: thinks it might be diabetic neuropathy
concerns: He is worried that his feet will develop sores that won't heal and lead to an amputation like his older brother had.
expectations: He hopes to get a soothing cream or a prescription to stop the burning sensation so he can finally sleep.
pmh: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed 12 years ago

clinical_knowledge.topic: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Diabetic Neuropathy: Duloxetine, Pregabalin, daily foot inspections, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to B12 deficiency without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Foot ulcers.
management_principles: Plan for Diabetic Neuropathy: Duloxetine, Pregabalin, daily foot inspections
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Chronic hyperglycemia causing microvascular nerve damage, producing burning pain and numbness in a stocking distribution on both feet.

must_ask.say: Is this in both feet, like wearing stockings?
How long have you had diabetes, and how controlled is it?
Do you check your feet daily for sores?
How is this affecting your walking or sleep?

history.answer: My feet have been burning and feeling numb for the past few months, and it seems to be gradually getting worse.
It feels like pins and needles with a burning ache and numbness, but my leg strength feels completely normal.
It affects both feet equally, starting down in the toes and coming up like a pair of short socks.
It is a constant tingling and burning sensation, almost like walking on hot sand or carpet with needles.
It started slowly about four or five months ago, not suddenly.
It began just in my toes and has gradually climbed up toward my ankles over the past few weeks.
It gets much worse at night when I take my shoes off and lie down in bed, and rest does not relieve it.
I can still walk and use stairs, but my feet feel somewhat clumsy because I cannot feel the floor clearly.
No, my hands and arms feel completely normal, and I have no trouble buttoning shirts or holding utensils.
No, I have no neck or lower back pain, and nothing shoots down from my spine into my legs.
No, my face has not drooped, my speech is normal, and I have had no sudden weakness, vision changes, or dizziness.
No, my bowel and bladder habits are completely normal, and I have no numbness around my groin or buttocks.
No, I have not had double vision, drooping eyelids, or any difficulty chewing or swallowing food.
No, I haven't seen any muscle twitches or shrinking in my calves or feet.
No, I have not had any stomach flu, diarrhea, or feverish cold recently.
I have been feeling generalized fatigue lately, but I have not had any fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss.
I have had type 2 diabetes for twelve years, and my last hemoglobin A1c was around 8.2 percent six months ago.
I try to check my feet every few days, and so far I haven't seen any open sores, cuts, or blisters.
I eat regular meals including meat and dairy, and I have never had stomach surgery or gastric bypass.
I am not taking water pills, chemotherapy, or steroids, just my prescribed diabetes medicine.
I am retired from desk work and do not do heavy kneeling, deep squatting, or resting on my elbows.
I only have type 2 diabetes, diagnosed twelve years ago; I don't have hypertension or high cholesterol.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I take metformin 1,000 milligrams twice a day, and I do not take any over-the-counter painkillers or supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only have a casual drink once or twice a month with friends, never heavy drinking.
I am a retired accountant and live at home with my wife.
My father had diabetes, but no one in my family had any nerve disorders or muscle conditions.
The burning pain makes it difficult to fall asleep at night, which leaves me worn out during the day.
history.topic: Impact on daily life and sleep

history.answer: I'm really scared that my feet might get infected and have to be amputated like my brother's did.
I'm hoping to get some kind of cream or medication to calm this burning down so I can sleep through the night.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute and regular, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Alert, oriented, and in no acute distress with normal seated posture.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial movements, normal extraocular motility, and clear articulation.
Normal muscle bulk and tone without fasciculations; strength is 5/5 across all major muscle groups in both upper and lower extremities.
Symmetrically decreased sensation to light touch, pinprick, and vibration below both mid-shins in a stocking distribution, with mildly impaired toe position sense.
Achilles tendon reflexes are absent bilaterally, patellar reflexes are 1+ bilaterally, and plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally with normal capillary refill.
Skin on both feet is dry without erythema, calluses, fissures, or active ulcers.
Normal casual gait and preserved heel-to-shin testing, with mild swaying on tandem walking and Romberg testing with eyes closed.
Full spinal range of motion without midline tenderness; straight-leg raise test is negative bilaterally.
